gates.median>=6: PASS. Recomputed median of {5,5,6,6,6,6} = 6.0, exactly at the threshold. Carried by four of six reviewers; the two 5s are R1 (increment/novelty) and R6 (headline adjudicated against an impeached reference). The gate is met but with no margin: one reviewer moving 6->5 would fail it.
gates.lower_quartile>=5: PASS. Order statistic, numpy method='lower': sorted[int(0.25*(6-1))] = sorted[1] = 5. Equal to the threshold, and it is the floor of the panel -- no reviewer is below 5, so this gate cannot be failed by any single reviewer here without a rating of 3 or 1.
gates.no_rating_of_1: PASS. Ratings are {5,5,6,6,6,6}; min = 5. No reviewer proposed strong reject, including R6, whose specialty was to assume the paper is wrong and which still returned 5 with ceiling 8.
gates.min_ceiling>=6: PASS. Ceilings are {6,8,8,8,8,8}; min = 6 (R1), median = 8.0. Every reviewer holds that the paper can reach or exceed the acceptance threshold with no new experiments. Note the ceiling distribution is where the panel actually splits (5-1 for 8 vs 6), and R1's 6 is a judgement about increment rather than about an unrepaired defect.

meta_rating_rationale: 6, marginally ABOVE the line, and I am picking a side rather than reporting borderline. Above, because I re-derived the load-bearing arithmetic myself and it is correct: all 27 BH q-values (qwen3/k14 q=0.0297, olmo2/keep14 q=0.0663, 6 cells at q<=0.05, 5 clearing Bonferroni 0.001852), P(X>=3|12,0.05)=0.019568, the exact-rational floors, the 9-of-25 off-MMLU numerator, McNemar 0.5702338863715973 from the shipped b=631/c=610, chi2=10.217 df=9, and the floor estimator's own sd=0.2446pp. The protocol contribution stands on its own, the self-falsification is real and costs the paper its largest construct, and every defect the panel names is closable with zero new measurement. Below 8, because the abstract's flagship 15/17 is adjudicated against a reference the paper itself impeaches four columns away in the same table (Floor 0.116606 vs E[f-hat] 0.113873), the arm-vs-floor bootstrap holds that reference fixed while the paper's central point is that it is a noisy maximum, and the released artifact cannot execute the verification story its own Reproducibility Statement describes.
consensus_strengths: Numerical reproducibility of the in-scope tables is exceptional and I confirmed it independently, not by trusting the reviewers: the 27-cell BH step-up reproduces every printed q to 4dp with 0 mismatches; the nine floors are exact rationals; the binomial, the 36-item/0.2992pp stratification slack, shortgpt16's 5.2x (3.6735/0.70229=5.231), 2532/14042=18.0316%, and the off-MMLU 9-of-25 numerator (5 shortgpt16 + 4 keep14, +6.47 to +49.66) all recompute. R5 additionally reimplemented the legality-aware null from the histogram alone and landed on 0.113876/0.117188/0.0833 against the paper's 0.113873/0.117188/0.083.

The self-falsification is real, load-bearing, and propagated to the abstract. The legality-aware correction moves the flagship MMLU-Pro row from p<1e-5 to p=0.083 and takes the survivor count from four to two; the abstract, intro and Table 1 all carry the weakened claim. The rounding sub-defect (comparing against a 6dp floor demands count 1404 when 1403 was observed, biasing p downward) is disclosed with the correct sign. The two ARC rows that moved in the authors' favour are printed rather than absorbed, explicitly to refute a blanket monotonicity claim the authors had made before measuring. All six reviewers credit this; none found a place where a favourable movement was absorbed silently.

Prior-art boundaries are drawn, not gestured at. Balepur (majority-class), Zheng 2025 (null model against judges), PriDe (predictor-side vs reference-side), OLMES (max-over-formulations), Oostermeijer (length normalisation) are each separated, and the v2 statistic is de-claimed as the numerator of Cohen's kappa with the option-count-aware chance-correction literature attributed claim by claim to Bennett/Brennan/Frary/Brenner/de Vries. The residual claim is narrowed to the within-stratum permutation for item-varying k plus its use as a gate.

The v1>=v2 ordering is stated as a measured property under a regularity condition, with the counterexample exhibited (per-stratum argmax B,E,B,E over 623 of 12032 items, slack exactly 36 items = 0.2992pp) and with the 13 of 27 cells that could not have violated it named, so the 27/27 empirical count is not oversold.

The v2 collapse-invariance is a shipped self-test, not an assertion: delta_perm = 0.0 for all ten always-L emitters, each conditioned on the items where that letter is legal (n_items 12032 down to 9981 for J).

Denominators are declared once and the paper's own prior violation is disclosed at the point of exclusion, naming the two omitted arms with their values (shortgpt16 +3.674 p=0.0001, keep14 +0.324 p=0.3234) and the reason the omission was indefensible (retained depth 14 was counted as damaged for the three non-OLMo families inside the same ratio).
consensus_weaknesses: ARTIFACT INTEGRITY, unanimous and the worst-placed defect in the paper. I confirmed seven named artifacts are absent from the frozen snapshot: tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md (the resolution target for 8 of Table 12's rows), evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json and evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json (the shipped claim_evidence_map.tsv names these as the SOLE sources for headline claims H-02 and H-04), code/gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py, code/gate_designated_denominator.py, evidence/mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json, evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json. code/ holds exactly five .py files. I ran the emitters in a copy of the snapshot: emit_tab_construct_nulls.py rc=1 (FileNotFoundError on e2_single_source_assertion.json), recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py --check-only rc=1 (FileNotFoundError on mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json), and check_prose_vs_evidence.py rc=0 printing '[scan] 0 files, 21 targets ... n_uncovered=12' because prose_files() globs PAPER/sections/*.tex while the snapshot ships manuscript/*.tex. A checker that returns PASS over zero inputs is the exact fail-open mode this paper says it guards against. MANIFEST.json asserts freeze_gate_pass true and named_artifacts_missing [] over 17 censused paths, with its own known_limitation conceding it checks presence and not currency.

THE REPRODUCIBILITY STATEMENT'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS UNSUPPORTED. It says a checker 'walks all numerals in the source' and 'reports 610 numerals with none unresolved'. The shipped checker has MIN_DP=3, a 21-target set built from floor/chance fields, and reports n_checked=65 with n_skipped=12. No artifact in the release records 610 or that check.

THE HEADLINE IS ADJUDICATED AGAINST A REFERENCE THE PAPER ITSELF IMPEACHES (R6 primary, R2 in CI form; the single most consequential objection). Table 1 prints Floor 0.116606, E[f-hat] 0.113873, q95 0.117188 for MMLU-Pro -- q95 EXCEEDS the observed floor -- and Table 5 then tests all 17 damaged cells against 0.116606 and never against 0.113873. My recomputation: against the raw floor 5 of 17 are above on the point estimate; against E[f-hat] 9 of 17 are; the shift is 0.27327pp. Separately, the arm-vs-floor paired bootstrap freezes the winning letter (code/mmlu_pro_trunc_fix_compare.py:51-54 computes bc_vec once on the full sample), so it propagates no selection uncertainty at all. I measured the reference's own sampling distribution at the observed marginal (200k multinomial draws, n=12032, seed 7): sd=0.2446pp, E[max]-observed=+0.0550pp, P(argmax!=A)=0.2307. qwen3/k14's 'statistically real' +0.233pp margin with half-width 0.191pp is smaller than one sd of the reference it is measured against, and llama2/k14 and k12 carry half-widths of 0.083pp that are arm-only noise. The paper cannot both make the winner's curse its contribution and treat the floor as known in every per-cell decision.

THE SURVIVING QUANTITATIVE CASE IS TWO LABEL-IMBALANCE CONSTRUCTS (R1 central, R2, R4, R5, R6 all concede the scope). After the paper's own correction only MMLU (fixed 4-way, 0.268908 vs 0.250000) and BoolQ (fixed 2-way, 0.621713 vs 0.500000) clear the realisable null; the other six sit at p=0.083-0.853, and on CommonsenseQA and PIQA the floor is BELOW E[f-hat]. R1's reading is that 'the majority-class baseline on MMLU and BoolQ exceeds nominal chance' is a computation over public gold labels that Balepur already frames and Arcon already reports, leaving a reporting recommendation plus a case study.

'POWERED' IS A 50%-POWER CRITERION (R2, R3, R6). power_verdict's criterion is 'achieved CI95 half-width < 1.389 pp'; half-width == effect is power 0.500 exactly. I confirmed 80% power needs hw <= 0.9717pp and the widest of the 21 MMLU-Pro cells is 0.9684pp, so the 21/21 claim survives by 0.0033pp of margin -- by luck, not design. The same criterion labels Table 4's MMLU (hw 1.154), ARC-Easy (1.305) and Winogrande (1.184) as detecting the effect at actual power 0.655/0.550/0.633.

THE ONE MULTIPLICITY-SURVIVING RESULT IS FAMILY-DEPENDENT (R1, R3, R6). Sec 5.3 calls the 27-cell family 'the one place in this paper where the family definition is not in dispute'. I recomputed: dropping the four intact-regime anchors (guaranteed rejections at p=0.0001, not damaged arms, not the subject of any tested claim) moves qwen3/k14 from q=0.0297 to q=0.0759 and drops the q<=0.05 count from 6 to 1; collapsing the five qwen3 heal checkpoints of one run sampled 500 steps apart gives q=0.0253. Both adjustments are defensible and they push in opposite directions, so both belong in print with the pre-registered family named.

THE SYMMETRIC-STANDARD FLIP HAS NO MULTIPLICITY-VALID FORM (R1, R2, R3, R6). Appendix A.4 correctly reports that under BH or Bonferroni neither reference retains a cell (0/12 both sides) and falls back on P(X>=3|12,0.05)=0.019568. Applied symmetrically the floor side gives P(X>=1|12,0.05)=0.459640, i.e. entirely consistent with the same global null. The abstract's '3/12 above chance versus 1/12 above the floor' therefore conveys a contrast the surviving statistic does not license; the honest form is 'the chance side is not uniformly null', which only the appendix says.

NUMBERS IN THE APPENDIX TRACE TO SUPERSEDED INTERMEDIATES (R2, R4, R5, R6; R4's diagnosis is the correct one). 03b_nulls.tex:37 prints ARC deltas of -0.0025 and -0.0063 'at roughly -17 and -23 standard errors'. The shipped record gives dp -0.0012050 at dp_sigma -3.339 and -0.0052133 at -7.336, with dE_max_sigma -9.775 and -17.749 and a top-level narrative giving a third pair. I located all four printed numbers verbatim in code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:78, inside a docstring describing an 8-seed x 1e6-draw run, while the shipped record is 3 seeds x 2e5 draws. The verdicts do not turn on it, but the paragraph exists specifically to make a directional-honesty claim auditable, and a -17 where the record says -3.34 is a 5x overstatement of distance from Monte-Carlo error. Relatedly, 03b_nulls.tex:22's 0.9003pp tokenizer split move is unsupported: the shipped four-tokenizer split spread is 0.4681pp (credit's 9.26 does check out at 9.2586).

SELF-CONTRADICTIONS IN THE PAPER'S OWN CHECKED ARTIFACTS (R1, R2, R3, R4, R6). I verified each: Table 10's caption asserts the two p columns 'agree by construction' where n_opt is constant, yet PIQA (n_opt_hist {2:1838}, n_opt_is_constant true) prints blind 0.658 vs legal 0.691 -- the evidence file's own p_change_attribution says 'threshold convention only', and its p_2x2 shows blind_exact_floor=0.691985 would agree, so the row mixes a second, unnamed axis. Table 5's caption says 17 cells, 09_appendix.tex:16 points at 'all 12 cross-family cells', and 14 rows are printed because Llama-3's four rungs collapse into one range row -- in the one family whose depth ordering is non-monotone (k14 -0.191, k12 -0.474, k10 -0.465, k8 -0.308). claim_evidence_map.tsv, shipped as E-K and asserted one-to-one with Table 11, still reads '14/15' at C-13 and 'only MMLU-Pro, MMLU, BoolQ survive' at H-03. mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:protocol.max_len is 1536 while Sec 4 and the Reproducibility Statement say 2048 and Table 11 row 14 prohibits the 1536 numbers (the data are the 2048 re-run; the metadata is stale), and mmlu_pro_power_nulls.json still ships with crossfamily {}.

THE MATERIALITY BAR IS APPLIED ASYMMETRICALLY (R2, and I confirmed the asymmetry runs in the direction that helps the thesis). The 0.10-of-anchor rule demotes qwen3/k14 at relative_recovery 0.09068, printed as 9.1%. olmo2/keep14 -- the cell promoted to TRACE_SIGNAL and discussed at length -- is at 0.02041/0.30447 = 0.06703, a clearer failure of the same bar, and that ratio appears nowhere in the prose. Nothing collapses (the upgrade does not survive BH at q=0.0663) but selective standards are precisely what this paper is built to prevent.

OFF-MMLU DENOMINATORS ARE 25/85 AUDITABLE (R1, R2, R3, R5, R6). gate2_letter_content_nulls.{json,csv} contains six arms, all OLMo-2 (grep for llama2/llama3/qwen3 returns 0). I reproduced the entire 9-cell numerator and the 0/15 at depth<=12 from those 25 cells, but the 60 non-OLMo cells exist in the snapshot only as pooled five-task rows that Table 11 row 9 forbids reading per benchmark, and the strings 9/85, 45/85, 25/60, 7/60 and 0/60 appear in no evidence file (only 52/60, in narrative prose).

PRESENTATION AND LIKELY DESK-CHECK RISK (R1, R4, R6). From the PDF: 26 pages, 0 images, 0 figure captions, and all 12 table captions on pages 14-26 while the text discussing them is on pages 1-9. Body text on page 10 runs from y=84.2 to REFERENCES at y=346.4 against a text bottom of 732.3, i.e. Section 7 occupies about 40% of page 10 (24 body lines, four paragraphs) -- roughly 9.4 main-text pages against ICLR's 9. main.tex:39-44 shows the authors know the exclusion rule (they moved Ethics and Reproducibility past the bibliography citing it); Limitations is not among the excluded sections. Separately, refs.bib has 17 entries and not one is a dataset or model paper, in a paper about how benchmark scores should be reported.

REVIEW-PROCESS LEAKAGE IN THE RELEASED ARTIFACT (all six flagged it; R6 logged it as a breach against itself and disregarded it). construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:why, emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:27, recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:6/482/865 and mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json all attribute the corrections to 'four of the six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6)', and MANIFEST.json:provenance_note gives round_04's snapshot hash. Two evidence fields also carry author-facing imperatives ('must not be printed', 'must NOT be described as well inside'). This is de-anonymising workflow provenance, not steering; every reviewer re-derived the correction independently. It must be stripped before submission.
disagreements_preserved: NO PAIR DIFFERS BY >=5 RATING POINTS. The spread is one point (two 5s, four 6s), so the panel does not disagree about what the paper IS. The genuine split is on the CEILING, and it is a 2-point split with a 5-1 vote: R1 alone says 6 (no amount of prose reaches 8; 'As it stands the paper's own corrections have left the reporting rule intact and the quantitative case thin, and I do not think prose can close that gap'), while R2/R3/R4/R5/R6 all say 8 and each name a purely editorial/CPU path to it. This matters more than the rating spread because it is a disagreement about whether the residual problem is packaging or substance. My adjudication sides with the five: R1's own list of ten changes to reach 6 is entirely editorial, and its stated barrier to 8 -- that only two fixed-k constructs clear the calibration -- is a scope limit the paper already states in its abstract and Limitations, not an unrepaired defect.

THE TWO DISSENTERS DISSENT FOR DIFFERENT REASONS AND ONLY ONE IS ABOUT THE PAPER'S CORRECTNESS. R1's 5 is a novelty/increment judgement: post-correction the positive content reduces to a majority-class computation over public labels plus a reporting checklist, thin for a main-conference slot. R6's 5 is a correctness judgement: the headline count uses a reference the paper's own calibration impeaches and the CIs propagate no selection uncertainty. These are not the same objection and they do not have the same remedy. R6's is closable by a table column and a sentence; R1's is not closable without new measurement. Both must survive into the decision rather than being averaged into 'borderline'.

R1 AND R3 COMPUTE THE SAME BH SENSITIVITY AND GET DIFFERENT ANSWERS; R3 IS RIGHT. R1: 'dropping the five intact anchors ... gives qwen3/k14 q=0.0759 and nothing at all surviving.' R3: removing 'exactly those four' gives q=0.0759 and 'the count of q<=0.05 cells drops from 6 to 1.' I recomputed: there are four intact-regime cells (qwen3, olmo2, llama2, llama3 INTACT); the fifth p=0.0001 cell is olmo2/shortgpt16, a DESIGNATED DAMAGED arm, and it survives the restricted family at q=0.0023. R1's q for qwen3/k14 is right and its survivor count is wrong. Preserved because the two readings support opposite conclusions about whether the paper's 'v2 re-sorts rather than rescales' claim has any multiplicity-valid support at all: under R3's (correct) computation it retains one cell, under R1's it retains none.

R1 LISTS THE PROSE CHECKER AS A STRENGTH WHILE R2/R3/R6 LIST IT AS A DEFECT. Both describe the same tool. R1 copied code/ and evidence/ into a tree with the sections at paperC/sections/ and got rc=0, PASS, 65/65/0 -- I reproduced this exactly (65 checked, 65 ok, 0 mismatch, 1 uncovered: the Winogrande control floor 0.504341). R2/R3/R6 ran it in the frozen layout and got a PASS over 0 files. R5 is the only reviewer who reports both halves and it is the accurate account: the substance is sound, the packaging is fail-open. Not averaged, because the two framings imply different fixes -- R1's implies 'nothing to do', R2/R3/R6's implies 'the verification story is vapour', and the correct fix is narrow: repoint prose_files() and make a zero-file scan a non-zero exit.

R2 AND R3 CALL THE CHECKER'S SUPERSEDED INPUT A SUBSTANTIVE FAILURE; I FIND IT A HYGIENE FAILURE. Both state that check_prose_vs_evidence.py:92 reads floor_winners_curse_calibration.json, the file explicitly superseded, and R3 concludes it 'validates prose against the withdrawn calibration'. The path claim is TRUE, but build_targets (lines 211-214) reads only that file's `floor` and `chance` fields, and I diffed all nine of each against construct_nulls_legality_aware.json: identical. The supersession changed E[f-hat], q95 and p, none of which enter the target set. So no prose was validated against a retracted number; the defect is that the checker will silently diverge the moment the two files disagree. Preserved because R3 names this as a condition for dropping to 5.

R5 (confidence 5, the only reviewer at that level, and the specialty owner for this question) is the most reliable voice on artifact completeness and reaches 6 with ceiling 8 -- i.e. the reviewer who looked hardest at the worst-affected dimension still puts the paper above the line and says every number it could check recomputed correctly. R6, hunting for the reason the paper is wrong, found a real structural inconsistency but supported it with three arithmetic errors (below). Weight accordingly.
false_reviewer_claims_found: R6-adversary, PRIMARY WEAKNESS: 'Thirteen of the seventeen cells have |Delta vs floor| < 0.2733 pp, i.e. smaller than the bias the paper itself measured.' FALSE. Recomputing every cell from the v2 CSV: 7 of 17 have |Delta| below 0.27327pp. The number 13 is the count of cells whose |Delta| is below their OWN CI95 half-width -- a different quantity. R6 repeats the 13 as a required abstract disclosure in what_would_change_my_score, so the error propagates into its remedy.

R6-adversary: 'At that scale only 7 of the 17 cells reach 80% power', immediately followed by an enumeration of seven cells at power 0.302-0.527. Self-contradictory and wrong in both directions. At R6's own floor-scaled effect (which I confirm as 0.6023pp) 6 of 17 cells reach power >=0.80 and 11 fall below; every cell R6 enumerates is in the FAILING set, and it omits four more that also fail (llama3/k14 0.283, llama3/k12 0.283, llama3/k10 0.298, qwen3/k12 0.788). Each individual power value R6 prints matches my computation to 3dp, so this is a labelling/counting error, not a modelling one -- but as written the sentence understates the number of underpowered cells while its rhetoric overstates.

R6-adversary: presenting '8/17 at-or-below' as the corrected form of the paper's '15/17'. The two counts are not on the same standard and R6 does not disclose the switch. 15/17 is a CI-verdict count (2 cells clear, 15 do not); R6's 8/17 is a POINT-ESTIMATE count. On point estimates against the raw floor only 5 of 17 are above, so the point-estimate analogue of the paper's number is 12/17, not 15/17. Applying the paper's own CI standard re-centred on E[f-hat]=0.113873 with the same half-widths, I get 5 cells clearing and 12 at-or-below. The underlying objection is valid and load-bearing -- the aggregate does move, and it moves against the paper -- but the honest magnitude is 15/17 -> 12/17, not 15/17 -> 8/17.

R1-novelty: 'dropping the five intact anchors ... gives qwen3/k14 q=0.0759 and nothing at all surviving.' Two errors. (a) There are FOUR intact-regime cells in the 27, not five; the fifth p=0.0001 cell is olmo2/shortgpt16, which is a designated damaged arm and the subject of a positive claim, so it does not belong in a set characterised as 'not the subject of any tested claim'. (b) With the four dropped, shortgpt16 survives at q=0.0023, so one cell survives, not none. R1's q=0.0759 for qwen3/k14 is correct. R3 computed the same sensitivity correctly (6 -> 1).

R2-soundness: 'Under that criterion a cell with half-width 1.388 pp has power 0.399 against delta=1.389 at alpha=0.05, not 0.80.' FALSE: it is 0.5006. This contradicts R2's own correct premise in the same sentence that half-width == effect certifies 50% power. R2's other power figures verify exactly (hw for 80% = 0.9717, power at 0.96836 = 0.8027, Table 4's 0.655/0.550/0.633).

R2-soundness: 'evidence/second_mc_benchmark_crossfamily/gate2_crossfamily_nulls.json, the latter being a hard dependency of the shipped checker (GATE2X, line 96).' FALSE. It is guarded by `if os.path.exists(GATE2X)` at line 257; the checker runs to completion without it, as R1's and my own successful runs show. R2 also attributes the mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json hard dependency to the checker; it is in fact a hard dependency of recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:360.

R3-stats: 'grep across all 17 paths finds no 4303-as-tie-count, no 2532-as-flip-count, no 18.03, no 0.5702 and no 0.0033', framed as leaving Sec 5.4 with no machine-readable home. The greps are correct as literal-string facts (I confirmed 2532, 4303 and 0.5702 do not appear as standalone tokens anywhere in evidence/ or code/), but the inference is wrong for the McNemar p and the flip rate: both are exactly derivable from shipped values. R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md:62 gives b=631 and c=610, from which the exact two-sided binomial McNemar is 0.5702338863715973, and 2532/14042 = 0.18031619. R5 states this correctly. The genuinely untraceable quantities are the 4,303 tie count, the 2,532 flip count as such, and the CI [-0.0064,+0.0033].

R6-adversary: on the two absent gate scripts, 'MANIFEST.json's own cited_path_source is sections/*.tex, evidence/... and code/..., so these two \texttt{...py} mentions were within its declared scope and were not caught.' FALSE as stated. The manuscript cites them as bare filenames (\texttt{gate\_designated\_denominator.py} at 09a_relocated.tex:24 and \texttt{gate\_bh\_27cell\_consistency.py} at tab_v2_full.tex:38), not as code/-prefixed paths, so they fall OUTSIDE the declared census scope. The manifest did not fail inside its own scope; its scope is too narrow. R6's remedy (extend the census to bare \texttt{*.py} mentions and to Table 12's targets, as R5 also asks) is right; the accusation that the freeze gate 'reports green on a snapshot missing the two scripts' misdescribes why.

R1-novelty: 'the only match for that digit string [610] in evidence/ or code/ is a line number in R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md:62.' Inexact on both counts: 610 occurs as a substring inside several stored floats (e.g. construct_nulls_length_unit.json's 0.22098976109215018), and at R7 line 62 it is a DATA value, the McNemar discordant count c=610, not a line number. R1's substantive point -- that no shipped artifact records a 610-numeral check -- is correct and I confirm it.

NOT FALSE, recorded because it was the failure mode of a previous round and I checked for it specifically: no reviewer asserted anything contradicted by its own enumeration in the way round_04 produced. R6's power sentence comes closest (its count contradicts its own list) and is logged above. Every other numeric allegation I tested held: the seven absent artifacts, the two emitter rc=1s, the 0-file checker scan, protocol.max_len=1536, the PIQA caption falsification, the Table 5 17/12/14 disagreement, C-13's stale 14/15 and H-03's stale three-constructs, the 0.9003 vs 0.4681 tokenizer spread, the ARC docstring provenance, the keep14 6.7% materiality ratio, the 25-of-85 off-MMLU auditability, the page-10 overflow, 0 figures, and 17 bib entries with no dataset or model paper.
smallest_changes_that_would_move_the_med: 1. REPORT THE 17-CELL TABLE AGAINST BOTH REFERENCES AND STOP TREATING THE FLOOR AS KNOWN. Add an E[f-hat] column (or a second Delta column) to Table 5, state in the abstract and at Table 5 which reference the headline count uses and why, and either propagate floor-estimator uncertainty into the arm-vs-floor intervals or say unambiguously that every per-cell decision is conditional on the observed floor whose own sd is 0.2446pp. This is the ONE change that addresses both dissenters: it is R6's named path from 5 to 6 and R2's named path from 6 to 8. Zero GPU -- a parametric bootstrap over gold labels already in the artifact. When you re-report, use the paper's own CI standard: I get 5 clearing and 12 at-or-below against E[f-hat], not R6's point-estimate 8/17.

2. MAKE THE ARTIFACT EXECUTE ITS OWN STORY. Ship or re-point all seven absent artifacts (EVIDENCE_PACK.md or replacements for Table 12's eight rows, s2_02 and s2_03 or new sources for H-02/H-04, both gate scripts, mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json, e2_single_source_assertion.json); repoint check_prose_vs_evidence.py's prose_files() at the released layout and make a zero-file scan exit non-zero (--strict as default); repoint CALIB at construct_nulls_legality_aware.json; and extend the freeze gate to census Table 12's targets, the TSV's evidence_ids column, and bare \texttt{*.py} mentions. Demanded by all six reviewers.

3. FIX THE REPRODUCIBILITY STATEMENT. Either ship the tool that produces '610 numerals, none unresolved' or rewrite the sentence to describe the checker that exists (21 targets, 65 sites, MIN_DP=3, 12 skipped). As it stands the paper's integrity claim is the one claim in it with no record.

4. RESTATE 'POWERED'. Relabel the criterion as 'the reference effect lies outside the achieved CI95' (which is what hw < 1.389pp encodes, and it is 50% power at the boundary), or recompute at a stated power target and print achieved power per row in Table 4. Note in passing that the 21/21 claim survives an 80% standard by 0.0033pp (0.9684 vs the required 0.9717), which is worth saying rather than leaving to a referee to discover.
